class.name: FellowHair3D
class.brief_description: Hair of strands: guide strands simulated on the CPU, many more drawn between them on the GPU with a hair shading model.
class.description: Hair for a character's head (FellowEngine milestone 124, decision 0248). Put it under a [BoneAttachment3D] on the head bone: its scalp is the cap of a sphere ([member scalp_radius] about [member scalp_center], in the node's space) from its top down to [member coverage], the face's side (-Z) left bare by [member forehead_angle] — or the painted faces of [member scalp_mesh]. [member guide_count] guide strands grow from the scalp, combed along it (down and back) and falling, in [member segments] segments of [member length]. They are simulated on the CPU each frame in [member substeps] substeps: their roots on the scalp as the node moves, the segments' lengths kept exactly, a pull back to the styled shape strongest at the root ([member stiffness]), gravity, [member damping], the scene's [FellowWind3D] with [member drag], and out of the scalp's sphere and the [member colliders] (spheres and capsules: shoulders, a collar). [member strand_count] strands are drawn, each between the three guides nearest its root (how far between them: [member spread]), along a Catmull-Rom curve through their points, as ribbons facing the camera at least a pixel wide (a thinner strand's coverage goes to its alpha, dithered: use TAA or FSR for smooth hair), [member root_width] thinning to [member tip_width]. The hair model: Kajiya-Kay's diffuse, a specular lobe in the light's colour and a broader one in the hair's ([member specular_shift], [member specular_strength], [member specular_sharpness]), light through it from behind ([member transmission]); darker at the roots ([member root_occlusion]) and on the strands under others; the light's shadows fall on it and from it, and with [member self_shadow] it shadows itself from the sun. Motion vectors follow the strands (the guides' positions go to the GPU in a texture of this frame's and the last frame's halves, each strand's instance data naming this frame's), so TAA and FSR see the hair's own motion. Far away fewer, wider strands are drawn ([member lod_distance]) and the hair is not simulated ([member simulation_distance]). Every hair node of a frame is stepped on the worker threads at once (what the step reads from the scene — the node's transform, the wind, the colliders — gathered on the main thread first). In the editor the styled shape is shown, not simulated.

method.name: get_global_stats
method.description: Returns every hair node's work since [method reset_global_stats]: [code]frames[/code], [code]group_usec[/code] (the main thread's time for all of them: preparing on the main thread, their steps on the worker threads at once, sending them to the GPU), [code]simulate_usec[/code] (the steps' time summed over the nodes: what one thread would spend), [code]upload_usec[/code], [code]simulated[/code] (the node-frames stepped), [code]self_shadow_usec[/code] (the [member self_shadow] maps' time summed over the nodes, on the worker threads; decision 0268). See decision 0250.

method.name: get_guide_points
method.description: Returns a guide's points, global, from the root to the tip ([method get_point_count] of them): the simulated ones in a running game, the styled shape in the editor.

method.name: get_guide_rest_points
method.description: Returns a guide's styled shape where the node is now, global: the points its simulated ones are pulled towards.

method.name: get_point_count
method.description: Returns a guide's point count: [member segments] + 1.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns [code]guides[/code], [code]points[/code] (a guide's), [code]strands[/code], and the last frame's [code]simulate_usec[/code] and [code]upload_usec[/code] (the guides' texture and the strands' instance data sent to the GPU), [code]simulated[/code] (whether it was simulated: not beyond [member simulation_distance]), [code]visible_strands[/code] and [code]width_scale[/code] (the level of detail's); with [member self_shadow], [code]self_shadow_usec[/code] (its map's last time), [code]self_shadow_lit[/code] (a light found), [code]self_shadow_min[/code] and [code]self_shadow_mean[/code] (the least and the mean share of the light a guide's point got).

method.name: reset
method.description: Puts the guides back in their styled shape where the node is now, at rest (after a teleport; a move of more than 1 m in a frame does it by itself).

members.member: [CollisionShape3D] nodes with a [SphereShape3D] or [CapsuleShape3D] the strands are kept out of (shoulders, a collar), besides the scalp's sphere.
How far the strands stay from the scalp's sphere and the colliders (metres).
How much each strand's colour differs from the others (a share of its brightness).
How far down the scalp's sphere the hair grows, as an angle from its top (degrees).
The radius of the strands' curls (metres; 0: straight).
The curls' turns a metre.
How quickly the strands' motion dies away (per second).
How strongly the air (the [FellowWind3D]) pulls the strands to its own speed.
The angle about the face's direction (the node's -Z) left bare: the hairline (degrees; 0: none).
Gravity on the strands, in multiples of the project's.
The guide strands simulated (more: the hair's motion in finer detail; each costs the CPU).
A guide's length (metres).
How much shorter than its guides a strand may be (a share of their length).

The distance within which every strand is drawn (metres, as through Godot's default 75-degree view: a narrower view counts as nearer). Beyond it a share of them falling with the square of the distance (the hair's size on the screen), at least [member min_strand_share], each drawn wider in proportion so that the hair covers as much (decision 0249). 0: every strand at any distance.
The least share of the strands drawn however far the hair is (see [member lod_distance]).
The hair's colour at the roots.
How much darker the hair is at its roots (the light the hair above keeps from it).
A drawn strand's width at its root (millimetres; a drawn strand stands for a few real ones).
The scalp's sphere's centre in the node's space (metres).

A mesh in the node's space the roots grow on instead of the sphere's cap (the head's mesh, or a scalp made for it): on its faces whose three vertices' colour's red is 0.5 or more (all its faces if it has no colours), by area, the guides spread evenly over them, the strands at random; the mesh's normals give the comb its start (decision 0249). The sphere ([member scalp_radius], [member scalp_center]) stays the head's collider and the styled shape's: fit it inside the head.
The scalp's sphere's radius (metres): the head's.
The seed of the strands' random roots and variations.
A guide's segments: its simulated points less one.

How much the hair shadows itself from a light ([member self_shadow_light]: directional, or an omni or spot light) (0 to 1; 0: off, the material without it). Each frame the guides' points are splatted into a deep opacity map across the light (cells twice the guides' spacing, 32 slices along the light): what a point's strands cover of a cell — its guide's share of [member strand_count], its segment's length, the strands' width and their tips' fade, the segment's sine to the light — summed from the side nearest the light gives each point's optical depth, and [code]exp(-[member self_shadow_density] × depth)[/code] the share of the light it gets. The strands take their guides' shares, and dim that light's diffuse and specular light and the light through them from behind by it. Computed on the worker threads with the simulation (about 75 µs a frame for 160 guides on one core). The light: [member self_shadow_light], or the scene's first visible [DirectionalLight3D]. See decision 0268.

How opaque the strands are to the light that crosses them, for [member self_shadow] (1: opaque strands; 0.5: a layer of strands that covers the light lets about 60 % of it through). Higher for dark hair, lower for fair hair.

The light the hair shadows itself from with [member self_shadow]: a [DirectionalLight3D], or (milestone 149) an [OmniLight3D] or [SpotLight3D] — its direction then the one towards it from the hair's centre, the map made for that direction (the light far against the head's size), the material dimming the light that is not directional within about 18 degrees of it; empty: the scene's first visible [DirectionalLight3D] (looked for again at most once a second while there is none).
If [code]false[/code], the hair keeps its styled shape, following the node.
Beyond this distance from the camera the hair is not simulated: its styled shape follows the head (metres; 0: simulated at any distance).
How narrow the hair's highlights are.
How far the highlights are shifted along the strand (the cuticle's tilt): the light's-colour highlight one way, the hair's-colour one twice as far the other.
The highlights' strength.
How far between its three nearest guides a strand's root may lie (0: on its nearest guide, in clumps; 1: anywhere between them).
How strongly the strands keep their styled shape at the root (0-1); the pull fades to nothing at the tip.
The strands drawn.
The simulation's substeps a frame.
The hair's colour at the tips.
A drawn strand's width at its tip (millimetres).
Light through the hair from behind it.
The scene's [FellowWind3D] on the strands, in multiples of its speed.
